coverage: Read native schematic and PCB values/connectivity; independently exported the schematic netlist and confirmed agreement with work/netlist/connectivity.json.
Inspected native ERC/DRC reports and execution records: zero reported violations, unconnected items or schematic parity issues within configured coverage.
Evaluated the specified ideal shutdown analytically and with ngspice 42; verified initial charge, grounded input, unloaded output and measured voltage.
Recorded commands, versions, assumptions and results in review-work/circuit/experiments/REVIEW.md and commands.json.

findings.condition: C1 initially charged to 1 V, /IN grounded at t=0, no external load, ideal passive components.

evidence.locator: Line 1: /OUT must be <= 0.01 V at 5 ms
C1 value 100n at line 955; R1 value 100k at line 1274
C1 pads at lines 209–225; R1 pads at lines 358–374; matching saved values at lines 107 and 256
Lines 163–176: R1 between /IN and /OUT; C1 between /OUT and GND
R1/C1 values, grounded input source, IC=1 and transient UIC

findings.mechanism: The only discharge path is through R1=100 kΩ into grounded /IN. With C1=100 nF, the time constant is 10 ms.
findings.reasoning: Vout(t)=1 V × exp(-t/(R1*C1)), giving 0.60653066 V at 5 ms, approximately 60.7 times the permitted voltage. The output reaches 0.01 V only after 46.05 ms. An independent transient simulation preserving the initial capacitor charge confirms both values. Passing ERC/DRC does not establish this timing behavior.
findings.title: Saved RC values fail the 5 ms shutdown voltage requirement

limitations: No hardware measurements or nonideal component analysis; tolerances, leakage, ESR, parasitics, ratings and qualification are outside the stated ideal scope.
Startup, reset, brownout and interface behavior beyond the specified shutdown condition were not evaluated.
Native ERC/DRC were inspected rather than rerun; configured ignored checks were not re-enabled.
No zone refill, fabrication review or exhaustive independent geometry analysis; board checks describe the saved fill state.
